correctness.rationale: From [L,L]=kz, reconstruct D(v)=Av+phi(v)z and D(z)=cz, with A+A* = cI, A²=A, c²=c and phi A+c phi=phi. In odd characteristic c=0 implies A*=-A and adjoint idempotence yields A=0 and phi=0. For c=1, image and kernel of A are complementary totally B-isotropic m-spaces, requiring split dimension 2m; conversely their projection works, with q^m phi choices. Counting ordered transverse maximal isotropic spaces gives [2 prod_{i<m}(q^i+1)]q^{m(m-1)/2}, hence the claimed exponent. A central shear kills phi; hyperbolic bases make all pairs isometric. Independently tested full projection identities in dimension 2 at q=3,5,7 and count 2q nonzero; this corroborates, not proves, the universal Witt argument. Derivation-space count q^{1+n(n+1)/2} follows skew-adjoint parameterization.
residual_risks: No independent formal verification of all finite-field orders or singular B; both explicitly outside scope.
Finite brute tests only n=2 with prime fields, not the full infinite-field theorem.

value.rationale: The split-versus-nonsplit Witt obstruction is a structural distinction unavailable in the alternating Lie case. Exact labeled finite-field rank counts and single conjugacy orbit resolve a natural, nontrivial classification problem for symmetric two-step Leibniz algebras; not just substitution in a known table.

final_claim: Over odd finite fields, a nondegenerate symmetric two-step Leibniz algebra V⊕kz has a nonzero composition-idempotent derivation precisely if dim V=2m and B is split hyperbolic. Nonzero count is 2 q^{m(m+1)/2} prod_{i=1}^{m-1}(q^i+1), each of rank m+1 and in one automorphism orbit; other types only have zero.
